To compute ${f}^{′}(x),$ we first make the substitution $u=2x$ and then we apply the chain rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{2}^{2x}\sqrt{{t}^{3}-t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}{\int }_{2}^{u}\sqrt{{t}^{3}-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

The integrand is continuous on $[2,u],$ and so by FTC II we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\cdot \sqrt{{u}^{3}-u} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x)\cdot \sqrt{(2x)^{3}-(2x)} \\  & =2\sqrt{8{x}^{3}-2x}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of ${f}^{′}(2),$ we substitute $x=2$ in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(2) & =2\sqrt{8(2)^{3}-2(2)} \\  & =2\sqrt{64-4} \\  & =4\sqrt{15}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
